Comparison of ORA and GSEA Workflows for RNA-seq Enrichment Analysis in R Introduction During DSFB1 course, I have learned how to perform ORA Gene Enrichment analysis for an RNA-sequencing experiment and applied it on the provided dataset for the final assessment. To further deepen my knowledge of RNA analysis, I want to learn how to perform another type of RNA-seq enrichment analysis: GSEA. In this self-study assignment, I want to: Learn how enrichment methodology affect the biological interpretation of RNA-seq data and compare the previous ORA results with a new GSEA analysis using the same DESeq2 dataset. Obtain a more complete picture of the previously used data. Background | Difference between GSEA and ORA Difference between GSEA and ORA: ORA uses a threshold-filtered list of significant genes, while GSEA uses all genes ranked by expression change. ORA is ideal for quick, high-magnitude gene lists, whereas GSEA excels at identifying subtle, coordinated changes in entire pathways. https://pluto.bio/resources/Learning%20Series/gsea-vs-ora-two-key-pathway-analysis-approaches-for-next-gen-sequencing-data Data description & Research question The data is obtained from this research. ## ── Attaching core tidyverse packages ──────────────────────── tidyverse 2.0.0 ── ## ✔ dplyr 1.2.1 ✔ readr 2.2.0 ## ✔ forcats 1.0.1 ✔ stringr 1.6.0 ## ✔ ggplot2 4.0.3 ✔ tibble 3.3.1 ## ✔ lubridate 1.9.5 ✔ tidyr 1.3.2 ## ✔ purrr 1.2.2 ## ── Conflicts ────────────────────────────────────────── tidyverse_conflicts() ── ## ✖ dplyr::filter() masks stats::filter() ## ✖ dplyr::lag() masks stats::lag() ## ℹ Use the conflicted package (<http://conflicted.r-lib.org/>) to force all conflicts to become errors Table 1: Sample metadata table GEO.Sample.id Cell.line Treatment Run.id GSM3393013 Fibroblast line 1 (CL1500023) BCLXL SRR7866699 GSM3393014 Fibroblast line 1 (CL1500023) BCLXL SRR7866700 GSM3393015 Fibroblast line 1 (CL1500023) ONECUT1 SRR7866701 GSM3393016 Fibroblast line 1 (CL1500023) ONECUT1 SRR7866702 Research question: Do ORA and GSEA lead to the same biological interpretation of ONECUT1-induced fibroblast transdifferation?
